scientific_object.title: Cross-type constraint failure coupling in text-guided 3D scene generation
scientific_object.question: After conditioning on ordinary instruction load and each constraint type's marginal difficulty, are constraint failures in a generated 3D scene still conditionally dependent across types, or is the apparent collapse explained by independent multiplicative accumulation?
scientific_object.irreducible_object: A generator-side cross-type failure-coupling residual over the four released LEGO-Bench constraint classes. The object is not that longer prompts, more constraints, or particular constraint classes are harder. It asks whether Floor Layout, Material Selection, Object Selection, and Object Placement failures co-occur beyond a same-information conditional-independent model that already receives generator identity, instruction length, total constraint count, metadata block, and flexible per-type difficulty terms.
scientific_object.exact_ex_ante_prediction: On held-out instructions, a preregistered cross-type interaction model will improve prediction of joint constraint failures over the conditional-independent null, and observed cross-type joint-failure probability will exceed the null expectation from calibrated marginal failure probabilities. The excess coupling should be larger in higher constraint-type-entropy instructions. If conditional independence explains held-out joint/holistic failure once the frozen controls are applied, the candidate is falsified.
scientific_object.strongest_same_information_baseline: A conditional-independent Bernoulli model using the identical generator identity, instruction word count, total constraint count, analyst-defined metadata block, and flexible additive main effects for each of the four per-type constraint counts to estimate each constraint's marginal failure probability; joint failure and holistic success are then predicted by multiplicative composition with no cross-type interaction.
scientific_object.prediction_disagreement: The conditional-independent null predicts that the dramatic holistic collapse follows from multiplicative accumulation of marginal constraint failures. The candidate predicts positive excess cross-type co-failure and held-out predictive value from interaction terms after those same marginals and load controls are supplied.
scientific_object.scope_boundary: This is an independently proposed cross-substrate object. It is not a reproduction of VWE-Bench, not evidence about VWE author outcomes, and not yet a causal mechanism claim. Constraint-type entropy is a moderator of coupling burden, not the scientific object itself.

substrate.benchmark_unit: one released natural-language scene instruction with manually decomposed constraints
substrate.secondary_endpoint_reason: Holistic success is a conjunction over all constraints and is therefore expected to have stronger floor/load effects; it cannot be the sole primary endpoint for the integration hypothesis.

condition_type_entropy.definition: Shannon entropy in bits over the four official released constraint types
condition_type_entropy.role: pre-outcome moderator/stratifier for future coupling residuals, not a standalone complexity law

strict_matched_f0.role: future bounded robustness/falsifier panel only if independently authorized

construct_preflight.metadata_parser_note: Released labels are bound to constraints by condition_idx, matching the official evaluator. Rows 121, 127, and 129 demonstrate that label list order itself is not a valid binding rule.

current_source_collision_review.direct_collision: LEGO-Eval already reports constraint-count complexity groups and per-type Partial Success Rate, so count-based degradation and type-specific average difficulty are not candidate contributions.
current_source_collision_review.cross_domain_strong_null: arXiv:2608.12426 reports approximately independent multiplicative constraint-failure accumulation in LLM instruction following; the 3D candidate must demonstrate residual coupling rather than assume it.
current_source_collision_review.method_collision: GraphDreamer and InstructScene already establish scene/semantic graphs as structured 3D generation priors; a generic structured-prompt or scene-graph intervention is not a standalone novelty claim.

candidate_generator_suite.note: Exact executable revisions, assets, provider/runtime dependencies, and output format compatibility must be frozen by a later substrate preflight. Naming a published comparison method does not authorize its execution.

future_analysis_contract_if_authorized.primary_population: all 130 released LEGO-Bench instructions for each independently qualified generator, with one binary validity outcome per released constraint
future_analysis_contract_if_authorized.strongest_null_model: fit marginal constraint-failure probabilities using generator identity, instruction word count, total constraint count, analyst-defined metadata block, constraint type, and flexible additive per-type load terms; compose marginals independently to predict within-instruction joint failures and Holistic Success
future_analysis_contract_if_authorized.candidate_model: add preregistered cross-type interaction terms to the same-information null and evaluate only on instruction-grouped held-out folds
future_analysis_contract_if_authorized.primary_disagreement_test: cross-type interaction model must improve held-out predictive log loss over the independent null and the observed cross-type co-failure residual must be positive relative to the product of calibrated marginal failure probabilities
future_analysis_contract_if_authorized.entropy_moderation_test: the independent-null residual should be larger for higher released constraint-type entropy after the frozen load/length controls
future_analysis_contract_if_authorized.robustness_panel: 11 disjoint metadata-only matched pairs frozen before per-case outcomes, exact on total constraint count and metadata block, within 10 instruction words, with at least 0.35-bit type-entropy contrast; compare independent-null residual rather than raw success alone
measurement_negative_controls: estimate evaluator-only cross-type coupling on the released human-curated scenes that were constructed to satisfy their instructions

where executable, re-evaluate a bounded subset with each constraint isolated in fresh evaluator state rather than inheriting previous constraint outputs; coupling that exists only under sequential evaluator context is measurement coupling, not generator coupling
future_analysis_contract_if_authorized.direction_lock: positive excess cross-type co-failure beyond the calibrated conditional-independent null, with larger excess under higher type entropy

falsifiers: The conditional-independent multiplicative model predicts held-out joint failures/Holistic Success as well as the interaction model within the preregistered uncertainty criterion.
Cross-type co-failure residuals are null/negative or are fully explained by marginal type difficulty, load, length, generator identity, and metadata block.

Any apparent coupling is reproduced on human-curated satisfying scenes or disappears when constraints are evaluated in isolated fresh evaluator state, indicating evaluator-induced dependence rather than generator-side coupling.
The pre-outcome entropy-matched robustness panel does not show the preregistered increase in independent-null residual at higher type entropy.
The official evaluator cannot provide stable per-constraint outcomes for the qualified generator outputs without changing the scientific object.

method_intervention.candidate_only: an information-equivalent typed/structured representation would be admissible only if it specifically reduces the preregistered cross-type coupling residual rather than merely improving average Success Rate
method_intervention.prior_art_boundary: scene-graph/semantic-graph conditioning is already established by GraphDreamer and InstructScene, so generic graph conditioning cannot be claimed as the new method contribution
method_intervention.forbidden_now: Do not design, tune, or run the intervention before formal Generator/ProblemGate admission.
